```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Demand evidence in A is direct and sourced. Two r/patreon posts show creators who already pay fees, complain about them, and say they are actively looking to switch. B's only reproduced demand signal is one LinkedIn comment from someone receiving a gift and asking out of curiosity, not someone stating a need.",
    "A's payer and price are concrete. Creators already pay published platform fees (Patreon 10% plus processing, Memberful $49/mo plus 4.9%), so pricing has a clear anchor in money already being spent. B's own brief says the category's observed ACV ($15k–$20k+/yr at Sendoso) implies enterprise-style selling, which is a poor fit for a solo founder. It also flags that the small founders B would target may lack budget for $30–75 per kit.",
    "A includes a sourced precedent: a non-technical founder plus one contractor reached ~$140K MRR and an exit. It shows the wedge can work with minimal staff, though it depended on a pre-existing niche audience. B offers no comparable success case.",
    "B's core operational risks are physical logistics: sourcing, warehousing, customs, breakage and address failures. The brief itself says AI agents don't solve these. B's 'case for' assumes an existing swag-fulfillment API but cites no source for one, so that part of the build path is unsupported.",
    "Both ideas face incumbents that already offer the exact mechanic. A's heavy compliance burden is a real drag. The brief notes it can be reduced via a direct-Stripe-account model like Memberful's, though that remains an open question rather than a confirmed path."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence is the weakest item. The single reproduced data point is a LinkedIn commenter who received Stripe's gift and asked which vendor was used, which the brief admits comes from 'someone receiving rather than needing to build it.' The 'seed HN quote' it mentions is never reproduced or linked, so it counts as missing.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. A wins mainly because B's demand and build-path evidence are thinner, not because A is strong. A is a crowded, commoditized market with SEO dominated by incumbents. It carries significant payments compliance and money-transmitter risk. Its only success case depended on a founder who already had an audience, which most solo builders lack. Hitting a paying customer in 90 days with A likely requires a specific niche with an audience the founder can reach directly."
}
```
